# About me

I'm Angelika Merkel, a biologist who moved into bioinformatics around two decades ago, when the field had neither defined training paths nor clear professional roles.

My career has taken me through genomics, epigenomics, large collaborative research projects, research computing, and eventually the leadership of a bioinformatics facility. Over that time, the work itself changed. What started largely with analysing biological data gradually expanded to include developing workflows and software, managing increasingly complex data, working with computational infrastructure, and thinking about reproducibility and how all these different parts fit together.

Looking back, this evolution in my own work reflected a broader change in bioinformatics. Scientific analysis is still at its core, but the systems around it have changed and are now just as important: how projects are organised, how data moves, how workflows are designed and maintained, how results remain reproducible, and how technical decisions affect research and the people doing it.

Much of my more recent work has involved connecting these different layers — biology, data, software, infrastructure, and, most importantly, the needs of researchers and clinicians. It is these connections that have shaped how I see bioinformatics today.

## This site

*Building Bioinformatics* is my attempt to put into writing things I have observed, experienced, or been thinking about over the years, as well as topics I am simply curious about and want to understand better.

I use the site to revisit things I learned along the way, catch up with areas that have evolved, and go deeper into topics that I previously encountered mainly while solving a particular problem. Writing about them is also a way of getting these thoughts out of my head, organising them, and understanding more clearly how the different pieces fit together.

The topics naturally reflect the practical and engineering side of bioinformatics: software engineering, reproducible workflows, research data management, FAIR systems, computational infrastructure, and the connections between them.

Some of this is based on experience, some of it is learning and revisiting, and some of it is simply trying to understand better how modern bioinformatics works as a whole.
